recent_posts.title: Militant masthead logo (r)evolution
recent_posts.summary: A retrospective look at how the Militant newspaper's masthead logo evolved from 1964 to 1997. The piece traces each iteration of the logotype — from an initial slab serif through various hand-drawn and sans-serif versions — noting specific typographic choices such as tittle shapes, kerning, tracking, crossbar asymmetry, and counter sizes. The author, who sold the newspaper as a teenager, reflects on the design decisions made over three decades without knowing who the designers were.

recent_posts.title: Eleventy in a Box—just add water
recent_posts.summary: A web designer shares how they built a personal starter system called 'Eleventy in a Box' to eliminate repetitive setup work across client projects. The system includes boilerplate CSS, layout systems, naming conventions, and modular feature packs (blog, changelog, portfolio, etc.) that self-install via a script. This approach reduces development time and frees up more time for design work, while still allowing each project to look visually distinct.

recent_posts.title: Last week in the studio (CW17-26)
recent_posts.summary: A freelance web designer shares their weekly studio update, focusing on a project for Codeboxx, a thermal printer and supplies company. The work involved creative art direction — recreating famous artworks like the Mona Lisa and The Scream using QR code textures of varying densities as shaders over painting reproductions. To address the challenge of dull product photography in the industry, animated graphics were created to represent product categories. The project is nearing completion with coding and launch planned for the following week.

recent_posts.title: How I designed an animated SVG-driven website for composer Begoña Pereda
recent_posts.summary: A web designer shares his process for building an animated SVG-driven portfolio site for film and video game composer Begoña Pereda. The post covers typeface selection methodology, SVG optimisation techniques (achieving under 12 KB for complex graphics), and a CSS-plus-JavaScript animation architecture where CSS handles continuous motion and JavaScript controls state based on user interaction or audio playback. Key design elements include animated cassette tapes and a reel-to-reel tape recorder that responds to music playback.

recent_posts.title: Last week in the studio (CW15-26)
recent_posts.summary: A web designer documents their studio work for week 15-26, focusing on creating animated SVG graphics for the Mountain Duck app website. The work involved building inline SVG illustrations with CSS animations and vanilla JavaScript, structured as collections of moving parts (bubbles, cogs, file icons). The approach prioritized CSS for motion and JavaScript only for timing and spawning logic, with iterative refinement to achieve natural-feeling movement.

recent_posts.title: How I designed an information-rich website for The Shared Homeland Paradigm
recent_posts.summary: Andy Clarke shares his design process for building an information-rich website for The Shared Homeland Paradigm, a political research project on Palestine-Israel. He walks through his typography selection process (settling on Bankside Sans by Dalton Maag), graphic concept development including topographical maps, a carefully considered color palette that avoids politically charged flag colors, and the use of Eleventy as the CMS. The post emphasizes story-led web design where layout, type, and graphics work together to communicate complex ideas.

recent_posts.title: I added a spring mode to my animated SVG landscape
recent_posts.summary: A web designer shares how they added a seasonal 'spring mode' to an existing animated SVG landscape without creating a separate version. The approach layers CSS and JavaScript on top of the same SVG: a static layer shifts colors (lighter clouds, blue sky, sandy rocks), while JavaScript toggles a spring-mode class and assigns randomized animation delays to flowers. CSS keyframe animations make flowers 'pop' into view with a slight overshoot for an organic feel. The implementation respects prefers-reduced-motion, showing flowers without animation for users who prefer it. The technique demonstrates progressive enhancement and reusable seasonal theming for SVG illustrations.

recent_posts.title: Last week in the studio (CW16-26)
recent_posts.summary: A weekly studio update from web designer Andy Clarke covering client work including animated graphics for Iterate, launching a musician's website for Ryan Knaggs, helping a friend set up an Eleventy-based wedding planning site, and adding a seasonal SVG animation to the Stuff & Nonsense homepage.

recent_posts.title: Using AGENTS.md to enforce personal coding preferences in AI tools
recent_posts.summary: A web designer shares how they use an AGENTS.md file to encode personal coding preferences into AI coding tools like Codex, eliminating the need to repeatedly correct AI-generated code. The post includes two example AGENTS.md files: a global one covering CSS formatting rules, semantic HTML, inline SVG, motion preferences, and British English copy, and a project-level one tailored for Eleventy projects covering structure, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and build verification guidelines.

recent_posts.title: A bold new website for the Academy of Scoring Arts
recent_posts.summary: A case study of the redesigned Academy of Scoring Arts website, a membership platform for composers and musicians. The redesign focused on bold typography using Bankside Sans by Dalton Maag, a restrained two-accent color palette, and modular editorial-inspired layouts on a 12-column grid. Key goals included improving content discovery, communicating membership value, and increasing sign-ups. The project was implemented in WordPress and emphasizes that intentional design decisions can make even conventional structures feel distinctive.
